promises.promise: Credentials agents need, and who may use each one. A secret is a named credential, such as a GitHub token.
Keeps each value encrypted, in a separate file held by a separate small program.
Lets an agent request a secret, and a person or a rule answer.
Grants access for a set time, to one agent or to one job.
Writes down every time a value is handed out.
A grant goes to one agent and can be limited to one job. Each use names the job.
A request records the conversation it was asked in.
A pending request waits in a person's Inbox.
Work can wait on the request with a trigger that fires when it is answered.
A connection's bot token is one of the stored secrets.
An agent requests a secret with a reason and a length of time. A person answers, or a rule answers for them. A yes creates a grant that lasts a set time.
A rule is a standing answer for one secret, for the agents it lists. Answering always makes a rule. The household has a default for a secret with no rule of its own.
A secret's value never sits in loom's main database. The app can set or replace a value and cannot read one back.
Every time a value leaves the key holder, loom records which secret, for which agent and job, and when. Each time a value is set, replaced or removed is recorded too.
a Owners manage them. Household owners manage Settings, which is where secrets, requests and grants are.
b Values are never shown. A value is write-only. Nobody reads one back in the app.
c Agents. An agent is handed a value only under a grant, and each hand-off is recorded.
d Checked at the door. Loom applies this to callers from outside: a person, an agent, a machine, someone's own program. Loom's own parts read without asking.
Secrets live in Settings with requests and grants.
The owner can add, replace and remove a Secret value in Settings; reload preserves the result, the value is not displayed or stored in the main database, and each change is recorded.
The owner can change the household default from Ask to Never in Settings and it persists after reload.
